headline: Bank of America strategists say the borrowing spree to build AI infrastructure is pushing up borrowing costs for developing countries by competing with governments for capital.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: only the opening paragraphs of the Bloomberg report could be read, so the evidence behind the strategists' view is unknown.
importance_line: What changed is a strategists' warning that AI borrowing is crowding emerging-market governments out of bond markets, which matters first to people in developing countries whose governments pay more to borrow, then to bond investors, then to AI builders issuing debt, and the doubt is that the rest of the analysis, its figures and the countries named are not known.
summary: Bloomberg reports that the debt-funded build-out of AI infrastructure is pitting governments against technology giants for capital, and that Bank of America strategists say this is driving up borrowing costs for developing nations, whose bond yields were already under pressure from geopolitical concerns, high oil prices and higher policy interest rates.
notes: Only the opening two paragraphs of the Bloomberg report could be read (paywall); no other outlet readable. Summary limited to the lead.
